title: Grade 7 Math — Tue, May 19
description: Probability — Day 2 of 5: Simple probability calculations
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A bag has 4 red, 3 green, 3 blue balls. What is P(red)?
Cards numbered 1 to 10. One is drawn. P(drawing card 5)?
Rolling a die: P(getting an odd number)?
questions.explanation: Odd numbers on a die: 1, 3, 5 → 3 outcomes. P(odd) = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.question: A bag has 2 white and 8 black balls. P(white) = ?
Cards 1–20 are shuffled. P(drawing a multiple of 5)?
P(getting number > 4) when rolling a die?
questions.explanation: Numbers > 4 on a die: 5 and 6 → 2 outcomes. P = 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.question: Cards numbered 1 to 10. P(getting a prime number)?
If P(red) = 1/4, what is P(not red)?
questions.explanation: P(not red) = 1 − P(red) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4. This is called complementary probability.

questions.question: A box has 5 letters: A, E, I, O, U. P(picking A or E) = ?
questions.explanation: Favourable = A or E = 2 letters. Total = 5. P = 2/5.

questions.question: P(getting even) + P(getting odd) when rolling a die = ?
questions.explanation: P(even) = 3/6 = 1/2 and P(odd) = 3/6 = 1/2. Together = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1. (Every outcome is either even or odd.)

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed. P(getting Tail) = ?
Rolling a die: P(getting a number less than 7)?
questions.explanation: All 6 outcomes (1,2,3,4,5,6) are less than 7. P = 6/6 = 1. This is a certain event!

questions.question: A bag has 6 balls: 2 yellow, 2 green, 2 red. P(yellow) = ?
If P(event A) = 0, what can you say about event A?
options: It may or may not happen
questions.explanation: P = 0 means the event can never happen — it is impossible.
